title: PATENT RESEARCH REPORT
abstract: This technical report synthesizes patent evidence for Hydrogenated Acrylonitrile NBR (HNBR), analyzing 12 primary patents published between 2009 and 2021. The research scope focuses on the catalytic hydrogenation of nitrile rubbers and the preparation of low molecular weight or functionalized HNBR variants. Key technical approaches include metathesis-mediated degradation using ruthenium-based catalysts (such as Grubbs, Hoveyda, and Arlt complexes) to control molecular weight, and heterogeneous catalytic systems (such as Raney Cobalt and supported Palladium) for hydrogenation and functionalization. Process trends reveal a strong emphasis on achieving low gel content (<5%), controlled Mooney viscosity, and introducing aminomethyl groups to enable alternative dianhydride-based crosslinking pathways. This report provides a comprehensive cross-patent comparison of reaction conditions, catalyst efficiencies, and resulting polymer properties.

patent_details.patent_title: Process for the preparation of hydrogenated nitrile rubber
patent_details.relevance_to_target: Compares hydrogenation performance of Grubbs II, Grubbs III, and Wilkinson's catalysts.

parameters.name: Reaction Time
parameters.context: Grubbs III hydrogenates faster in first 120 min

experimental_evidence: Grubbs III catalyst at 0.057 phr (65.6 ppm metal) achieved 0.4% residual double bonds (RDB) after 120 min.
Wilkinson's catalyst at 0.06 phr achieved 3.1% RDB after 120 min.
Mooney viscosity of the resulting HNBR ranged from 20.2 to 69.3 depending on the catalyst and degradation.
primary_patents.technical_relevance: Demonstrates that Grubbs III catalyst provides faster hydrogenation kinetics than Grubbs II or Wilkinson's catalyst at equivalent metal contents.

patent_details.patent_title: Process for the preparation of hydrogenated nitrile rubber
patent_details.relevance_to_target: Equivalent to US9079979, detailing hydrogenation profiles and catalyst comparisons.

experimental_evidence: Grubbs III catalyst (HNBR 1) achieved 0.4% RDB in 120 min compared to 3.1% for Wilkinson's (HNBR 3).
Mooney viscosity of HNBR 1 was 38.2, while HNBR 3 was 69.3.
Grubbs III catalyst hydrogenates faster in the first 120 min than Grubbs II or Wilkinson's catalyst.
primary_patents.technical_relevance: Confirms the superior hydrogenation efficiency of Grubbs III metathesis catalysts in European jurisdictions.

patent_details.patent_title: Process for the preparation of low molecular weight hydrogenated nitrile rubber
patent_details.relevance_to_target: Focuses on low molecular weight HNBR preparation using Hoveyda and Arlt catalysts.

experimental_evidence: Hoveyda catalyst at 0.041 phr achieved 0.6% RDB in 120 min and 0.4% RDB in 240 min.
Arlt catalyst at 0.045 phr achieved 4.5% RDB in 120 min and 3.5% RDB in 240 min.
Hoveyda catalyst (HNBR 1) yielded a Mooney viscosity of 33.3 and PDI of 2.34 after 240 min.
primary_patents.technical_relevance: Shows that Hoveyda-type catalysts perform more efficiently in terms of hydrogenation and molecular weight reduction than Arlt or Wilkinson's catalysts.

patent_details.patent_title: Process for the preparation of low molecular weight hydrogenated nitrile rubber
patent_details.relevance_to_target: Details the dissolution and high-pressure hydrogenation process parameters for low molecular weight HNBR.

parameters.name: Dissolution Time
parameters.context: Dissolved in monochlorobenzene at room temperature

experimental_evidence: 518 g of nitrile rubber was dissolved in 4300 g of monochlorobenzene (12% solution) over 12 hours.
Hydrogenation was conducted at 138 °C and 85 bar pressure.
Hoveyda catalyst (0.041 phr) achieved 0.4% RDB after 240 min, yielding a polymer with Mw of 113,371 g/mol and Mooney viscosity of 33.3.
primary_patents.technical_relevance: Provides complete process parameters for dissolving NBR and executing high-pressure catalytic hydrogenation to obtain low molecular weight HNBR.

patent_details.patent_title: Method for producing hydrogenated nitrile rubber and hnbr compositions thereof
patent_details.relevance_to_target: Focuses on improving the aging properties of HNBR using supported catalysts and specific vulcanization conditions.

parameters.name: Vulcanization Time
parameters.context: Typically 1 min to 24 hours, preferably 2 min to 1 hour

experimental_evidence: Gel content of crude polymers increased by less than 10% during aging for 4 days at 140 °C.
Mooney viscosity increased by less than 40% during aging for 4 days at 140 °C.
Ruthenium compounds in the range of 10 ppm to 200 ppm showed only a small influence on polymer aging.
primary_patents.technical_relevance: Discloses methods to produce HNBR with improved thermal aging resistance, characterized by minimal gel content and Mooney viscosity increases.

patent_details.patent_title: Hydrogenated nitrile rubber containing aminomethyl groups, method for producing …
patent_details.relevance_to_target: Introduces aminomethyl groups into HNBR to enable alternative crosslinking chemistry.

experimental_evidence: Raney Cobalt catalyst (Grace 2724) was pretreated by washing with methanol and THF to remove water.
Hydrogenation of Therban 3406 with ammonia (20 g) at 130 °C and 120 bar yielded 2.4 wt% aminomethyl groups and a gel content of 2.4%.
Crosslinking with pyromellitic dianhydride (26.3 phr) and DBU (2.21 phr) at 170 °C yielded vulcanizates with high tensile strength (27.1 MPa) and microhardness (83 IRHD).
primary_patents.technical_relevance: Enables the synthesis of aminomethyl-functionalized HNBR with low gel content, which can be crosslinked using dianhydrides instead of peroxides or sulfur.

patent_details.patent_title: Hydrogenated nitrile rubber containing amino methyl group and method for …
patent_details.relevance_to_target: Equivalent or closely related to EP2918612, detailing aminomethyl functionalization and crosslinking.

experimental_evidence: Therban 3406 was hydrogenated using pretreated Raney Cobalt and ammonia at 130 °C and 120 bar, achieving 11.6% nitrile conversion (2.2 wt% aminomethyl content).
Addition of n-dodecyl sulfide (0.1 wt% relative to catalyst) improved conversion and controlled gel formation.
Crosslinking with maleic anhydride at 180 °C for 2 hours achieved a gelation degree of 57.1% to 68.4%.
primary_patents.technical_relevance: Confirms the reproducibility of aminomethyl functionalization of HNBR and demonstrates crosslinking with cyclic anhydrides like maleic anhydride.

patent_details.patent_title: Low molecular weight hydrogenated nitrile rubber
patent_details.relevance_to_target: Describes simultaneous metathesis degradation and hydrogenation of NBR to produce low molecular weight HNBR.

experimental_evidence: NBR rubber (200 g) was dissolved in 1133 g of MCB to form a 15 wt% solid solution.
Metathesis degradation in the presence of ethylene (500 psi) at 80 °C reduced Mn from 85 kg/mol to 27 kg/mol and Mw from 296 kg/mol to 54 kg/mol.
1-hexene (150 g) was also successfully used as a co-olefin for degradation.
primary_patents.technical_relevance: Establishes a process for preparing low molecular weight HNBR via olefin metathesis degradation using co-olefins like ethylene or 1-hexene.

patent_details.patent_title: Low molecular weight hydrogenated nitrile rubber
patent_details.relevance_to_target: Equivalent to US7951875, detailing metathesis degradation parameters.

experimental_evidence: NBR rubber (75 g) was dissolved in 1175 g of MCB to form a 6 wt% solid solution.
Metathesis degradation with 1-hexene (150 g) at 80 °C successfully reduced molecular weight.
Resulting polymers exhibited narrow polydispersity index (PDI) and significantly reduced Mooney viscosity.
primary_patents.technical_relevance: Confirms the viability of using alternative co-olefins (e.g., 1-hexene) and lower solution concentrations (6 wt%) for controlled NBR degradation.

patent_details.relevance_to_target: Focuses on compounding HNBR with specific fillers and crosslinking agents for LLC resistance.

experimental_evidence: Compositions using 150 parts of MT carbon black and 6 parts of cocrosslinking agent showed excellent LLC (long-life coolant) resistance.
Silica (30 to 300 parts) and silane coupling agents (0 to 5 parts) can be used to achieve similar performance.
Roll processability was rated as excellent or good for the optimized filler and crosslinker ratios.
primary_patents.technical_relevance: Provides compounding formulations for HNBR to achieve superior resistance to long-life coolants (LLC) and good roll processability.

cross_patent_comparison: Catalyst Selection: Metathesis-based ruthenium catalysts (Grubbs II/III, Hoveyda, Arlt) are preferred for simultaneous degradation and hydrogenation to produce low molecular weight HNBR, whereas Raney Cobalt is utilized for functionalization (aminomethylation) and supported Pd is used for standard hydrogenation.

Process Conditions: Hydrogenation temperatures typically range from 80 °C to 160 °C, with pressures varying widely from 500 psi (approx. 34 bar) for metathesis degradation up to 120 bar for Raney Cobalt-catalyzed aminomethylation.

Molecular Weight Control: Metathesis degradation processes successfully reduce the weight-average molecular weight (Mw) from ~296 kg/mol down to ~54 kg/mol, significantly lowering Mooney viscosity to improve processability.

Functionalization and Crosslinking: Aminomethyl-functionalized HNBR (1-5 wt% amine content) enables alternative crosslinking with dianhydrides (e.g., pyromellitic dianhydride) at 170-180 °C, achieving high tensile strength (up to 27.1 MPa) without peroxide or sulfur.
conclusion: The patent landscape for Hydrogenated Acrylonitrile NBR (HNBR) reveals a strong focus on process optimization, molecular weight reduction, and functionalization. Metathesis degradation using ruthenium-based catalysts (Grubbs, Hoveyda) is a dominant trend for producing low molecular weight HNBR with improved processability. Additionally, aminomethyl functionalization using Raney Cobalt catalysts introduces novel crosslinking pathways via dianhydrides, offering peroxide-free vulcanization options. Gaps in the disclosed patent data include detailed long-term dynamic mechanical properties and specific emulsifier/stabilizer formulations used during the initial polymerization stage.
